clue.text: Pottery fragment revealed by spades with effort

parts.note: S is the card-game abbreviation for spades
doing something hard is doing it with effort, as in 'work hard'

explanation.surface: A digger's spade, worked strenuously, turns up a broken piece of pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: A shard is a broken piece of pottery or glass, a term archaeologists use for such finds.

clue.text: Start to spread news about obstruction and close off precarious situation

indicators.note: the start to a word is its first letter

parts.note: word means news, as in 'any word?'
of means about, as in 'tales of the sea'
a dam is an obstruction across a river

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gossip about a blockage gets spread around before a road is shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges CLOSE into OCLES. 'close off' reads as one verb, but off is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The sword of Damocles hung over a courtier by a single hair, an idiom for an ever-present threat.

clue.text: Language of extreme letters brought up passion

parts.note: A and Z are the letters at the two ends of the alphabet

indicators.note: brought up suits a down clue: the word is read upwards

parts.note: ire is anger, a passion

explanation.surface: A tongue made of the outermost letters rises with feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Azeri is the Turkic language of Azerbaijan.

clue.text: Raised edges of teak in modelled work surface

indicators.note: raised suits a down clue: everything is read upwards
in says the edges go inside the other word

parts.note: to model is to pose, so modelled is posed

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A carved worktop has raised teak edges.
explanation.walkthrough: TK goes into POSED to make POTKSED, which 'Raised' turns upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A desktop is the working surface of a desk, or a computer screen's main area.

clue.text: Late hours happening before about the middle of the month

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the second in the answer

parts.note: an event is a happening or occurrence

parts.words: about the middle of the month
parts.note: the ides fall on the 13th or 15th of the Roman month, roughly its middle

explanation.surface: Something is scheduled for the late hours on a date near mid-month.
explanation.walkthrough: The ides is the Roman name for the 15th (March, May, July, October) or the 13th of other months, hence 'about the middle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is an old poetic word for evening, so its plural names the late hours of the day.

clue.text: Board member direct from financial district

parts.note: ex means direct from, as in goods sold ex works
EC is the postcode of the City of London, its financial district

explanation.surface: A director arrives straight from the City.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postcode area covering the City of London, Britain's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Exec, short for executive, is a company director who sits on the board.

clue.text: Is dying to confess without one's verbalising

indicators.note: without says the letter for one is left out

parts.note: expires means is dying
I is the Roman numeral for one
to sing is slang for confessing to police

explanation.surface: Someone is desperate to own up, but not alone in saying so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is dying to confess' reads as eager to own up; it is EXPIRES, which loses I, and SING, criminal slang for confess.
explanation.definitionFit: Expressing something is putting it into words, which is verbalising it.

clue.text: Grass costs UK bucks

indicators.note: bucks, as a horse bucks, throws the letters about

explanation.surface: Greenery is expensive for British consumers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bucks' looks like dollars in a surface about costs, but it rearranges COSTSUK.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussock is a clump or tuft of coarse grass.

clue.text: Involving muck but little brass?

parts.note: read literally, something consisting of filth yet costing hardly any money, brass being northern English slang for money

explanation.walkthrough: 'Where there's muck there's brass' is a northern English saying: brass is money.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirt cheap means extremely inexpensive, an idiom joining filth with low price.

clue.text: Be overformal or obdurate, with former sign of dreaming being suppressed

indicators.note: being suppressed says the pieces are held down inside the stubborn word

parts.note: stony means hard-hearted, obdurate
and means with, joining things
once means former, as in 'the once king'
REM, rapid eye movement, happens during dreaming sleep

explanation.surface: Someone is either stiff with etiquette or stubborn, having once had dreams crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being suppressed' is the container signal; 'sign of dreaming' looks like part of the surface story but stands for rapid eye movement.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand on ceremony is to insist on formal behaviour, being overly formal.

clue.text: Elopers've exercised and wake up late

indicators.note: exercised suggests putting the letters through their paces, so they are reworked

explanation.surface: A runaway couple, having worked out, sleep in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercised' rearranges the nine letters of ELOPERSVE; the apostrophe adds nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversleep is to sleep past the intended time and so to wake later than planned.

clue.text: Land recalled in fairy stories

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A country is remembered in the old tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns AIRYS, which spans 'fAIRY Stories', round.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a country in the Middle East, and country is a sense of land.

clue.text: Delicacy surrounding one hollow night with its opposite

indicators.note: surrounding says the opposite of night goes around the other pieces

parts.note: the opposite of night is day
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: a hollow word has its inside emptied, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A tasty morsel encloses a single empty night along with daytime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' points back to night, so the opposite is daytime; 'hollow' empties night down to its first and last letters, and 'surrounding' wraps them and the one.
explanation.definitionFit: A dainty is a small delicacy or titbit, an old noun sense of the word.

clue.text: Celebrated about vocal support from the floor?

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters

indicators.note: vocal says the word for the floor support is spoken, and its sound is what goes in

parts.note: a joist is a beam that holds up a floor

explanation.surface: A speaker celebrates the cheers coming from the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support from the floor' looks like shouts of backing from an audience, but it is a joist, a timber beneath floorboards.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejoice is to celebrate with gladness, so the past tense matches celebrated.

clue.text: Business owner favouring publicity that is directed at resistance

parts.note: pro means in favour of
PR is public relations, publicity
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is
to means towards, directed at
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper backs advertising aimed at overcoming opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: A proprietor owns a business such as a shop or hotel.

clue.text: Defensive structures to protect Republican article and not hinder members

indicators.note: to protect says the defensive structures wrap around the other pieces

parts.note: forts are defensive structures
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Fortifications guard a political article, and the limbs move freely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to protect' is the container signal. 'not hinder members' reads as letting someone move freely, but it means front limbs as opposed to hind ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreparts are the front parts or limbs of an animal, the opposite of the hind ones.

clue.text: Restore assistant covering transgression up

indicators.note: up suits a down clue: the whole is read upwards
covering says the assistant goes around the wrongdoing

parts.note: a helper is an assistant
a sin is a transgression

explanation.surface: Bring back an aide who has covered up wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' puts the wrongdoing inside the aide, and 'up' then turns the whole run round, as suits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To replenish is to fill up again, restoring a supply.

clue.text: German mathematician with no capacity for the bottle?

definitions.text: German mathematician with no capacity for the bottle?

parts.words: German mathematician with no capacity for the bottle?
parts.note: a German mathematician gave his name to a bottle-shaped surface with no inside, so it can hold nothing

explanation.surface: A German scholar who cannot hold his drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Felix Klein described the Klein bottle, a one-sided surface with no inside: 'no capacity for the bottle' looks like being unable to hold drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Felix Klein was a German mathematician famed for geometry and the one-sided bottle named after him.

clue.text: Gelatin product used for photograph

parts.note: as means used for or serving as, as in 'a box as a table'
pic is short for picture, a photograph

explanation.surface: Gelatin is a material used in making photographs.
explanation.walkthrough: Gelatin really was used in photographic film, so the surface reads as fact.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made with gelatin, used to set meats and eggs.

clue.text: A team wearing black diamonds with one line shielding another

indicators.note: wearing says the pieces sit inside, as clothes are worn round a body

parts.note: black diamonds is a nickname for coal
XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A squad sports black diamond jewellery while one player protects another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black diamonds' is a fanciful name for coal; 'line' is a cable or wire.
explanation.definitionFit: A coaxial cable has an inner conductor shielded by an outer one sharing its axis.

clue.text: Attach peel loosely round a soft fruit

parts.note: to pin something is to attach it

indicators.note: round says the rearranged letters go around the other pieces
loosely suggests the letters of peel hang free and rearrange

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft

explanation.surface: Fix some loose peel around a squashy piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loosely' turns PEEL into EPLE, which 'round' wraps around A and P. 'soft fruit' looks like one phrase, but soft is P.
explanation.definitionFit: The pineapple is a tropical fruit with a tough skin and sweet yellow flesh.

clue.text: Insulting coach, I have to support ace

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting pieces sit below the ace

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace
a coach is a bus
've is the short form of have

explanation.surface: A rude coach backs a star player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' looks like a trainer, but it is a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: Abusive means insulting, using coarse or hurtful language.

clue.text: Ring, by means of stirring Act I, is this

definitions.text: Ring, by means of stirring Act I, is this

parts.note: O is shaped like a ring
per means by means of, as in 'per post'

indicators.note: stirring mixes the letters up

explanation.surface: Wagner's Ring cycle, with its rousing first act, belongs to a particular art form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirring' rearranges ACTI into ATIC. Read whole, the clue says Wagner's Ring, by virtue of a rousing Act I, is operatic.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's Ring is a cycle of four operas, so it is operatic, in the manner of opera.

clue.text: This tart is the reverse of chic, according to talk

indicators.note: according to talk says only the spoken sounds count, not the spelling

parts.note: chic is said 'sheek'; turning those sounds round gives 'keesh'

explanation.surface: A pastry is described as the opposite of stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal is of sounds, not letters: 'sheek' backwards is 'keesh'. The surface suggests an unfashionable tart.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiche is a savoury open tart filled with egg custard.

clue.text: Smoke Channel Islands fish

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands, British islands off France
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: Smoked fish from the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigar is something smoked, so it can be called a smoke.

clue.text: Whip female out of priesthood?

parts.note: lay people are those outside the clergy

explanation.surface: A woman is thrashed and expelled from holy orders.
explanation.definitionFit: To flay is to whip or lash severely, stripping the skin.

clue.text: Pirandello perhaps flouting his Six Characters individually being lost

indicators.note: losing six single letters, every other one, leaves alternate letters of the words before

explanation.surface: Pirandello is defying his famous play by having its characters vanish one by one.
explanation.walkthrough: Pirandello wrote 'Six Characters in Search of an Author'. Dropping six letters of FLOUTINGHIS one at a time (F, O, T, N, H, S) leaves the alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Luigi Pirandello was the Italian playwright, so Luigi is an example of a Pirandello first name.

clue.text: Earful of Nabucco, say, in tenor's opening with higher voice

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
in says the king is put inside the higher voice

parts.note: alto is a voice higher than tenor
Nabucco, Verdi's Nebuchadnezzar, is an example of a king

explanation.surface: An opera singer gets an earful at the start of a tenor's aria from a soprano.
explanation.walkthrough: Nabucco is Verdi's opera about the Babylonian king Nebuchadnezzar; 'say' marks him as one example of a king.
explanation.definitionFit: A talking-to is a scolding, the sort of telling-off also called an earful.

clue.text: Learned about short break aboard South Africa railway

indicators.note: aboard says the pieces get on inside South Africa

parts.note: c is short for circa, Latin for about
hol is a short form of holiday, a break

explanation.surface: An expert is travelling for a brief holiday on a South African train.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned (two syllables) means scholarly, showing deep knowledge from study.

clue.text: Lustrous, apart from first thing in the morning?

indicators.note: apart from first says the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: pearly means lustrous, with the sheen of a pearl

explanation.surface: Something gleams, except at daybreak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first thing in the morning' looks like a single phrase, but 'first' belongs to the deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: Early means in the morning, near the start of the day; the question mark admits it is one example of earliness.
